title: ORCHID-SAGE: Fully Reproducible CALPHAD Assessment from Evidence to Phase Diagram
abstract: arXiv:2611.16308v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Knowledge of phase stability is the first requirement for materials design, and predicting the conditions under which new materials can be synthesized has become a key capability of self-driving laboratories (SDLs). For inorganic materials, notably alloys, these predictions come from thermodynamic databases built with the CALPHAD method. Building a database, however, requires expert judgment at many steps, and because these decisions are rarely recorded, others can use a database but cannot regenerate or update it. Machines can already collect the data, build a first model with machine-learned interatomic potentials and refine it against experiments. The assessment itself, the sequence of judgments that turns these parts into a reliable database, is still carried out by human experts. translated_title: ORCHID-SAGE：从证据到相图的完全可复现CALPHAD评估
translated_abstract: 相稳定性知识是材料设计的首要要求，而预测新材料的合成条件已成为自动驾驶实验室（SDLs）的一项关键能力。对于无机材料，特别是合金，这些预测依赖于用CALPHAD方法构建的热力学数据库。然而，构建数据库需要在许多步骤中进行专家判断，由于这些决策很少被记录下来，其他人虽然可以使用数据库，却无法重新生成或更新它。机器如今已经能够收集数据、利用机器学习原子间势构建初始模型，并根据实验对其进行修正。而评估本身——即将这些组成部分转化为可靠数据库的一系列判断——仍然由人类专家完成。我们认为，只有将评估背后的专家知识编码到正式协议中，评估才能实现可复现的自动化，从而使评估得以……（摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文提出ORCHID-SAGE框架，通过将CALPHAD评估背后的专家判断编码为正式协议，实现了从证据收集到相图构建的完全可复现的自动化热力学数据库评估。
en_tdlr: The paper proposes ORCHID-SAGE, a framework that enables fully reproducible automated CALPHAD assessment by encoding expert judgment into formal protocols, spanning from evidence collection to phase diagram construction.
